function: MATD3 actors jointly choose UAV-MU association, UAV mobility, uplink bandwidth allocation, CPU allocation and offloading ratio to minimize MU energy; bandwidth allocation is the physical-layer part (pp. 5, 8).
system: Multi-UAV edge servers (2-6 UAVs) serving ground MUs; TDD, FDMA uplink, bandwidth 40 MHz; antenna configuration and carrier frequency not stated; no RIS (pp. 4, 10).
method: Multiagent TD3 (MATD3) with message, coordination (attention) and solution NNs, parameter sharing; centralized offline training, decentralized execution; reinforcement learning (pp. 8-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: MUs random in 100 m x 100 m, Gauss-Markov mobility, air-to-ground channel model of [1], [39], noise -130 dBm/Hz; no dataset (pp. 3-4, 10).
test_conditions: Trained with 3.0e6 episodes with 2-4 active UAVs of 6; tested on 1e4 independent episodes with M in [2, 6], including 5-6 UAVs unseen in training (pp. 10-11).
baselines: Non-learned: Naive (random matching, equal bandwidth and CPU); learned: vanilla MATD3 [43], MATD3 without initial message [34], without temporal message, centralized TD3 [41]; MASAC, MAPPO backbones (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Average total energy consumption of MUs, versus number of UAVs, message dimension, UAV CPU frequency, and system bandwidth; training convergence curve; UAV trajectories (pp. 10-13).
complexity: none; only a qualitative statement that attention cost is negligible (p. 7); layer widths listed (p. 10) but no parameter count, FLOPs or runtime.
q1_support: p. 4: "follows the air-to-ground channel model in [1] and [39]", a published analytical UAV model of the authors' own simulator, not a 3GPP, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model; p. 10: "Our simulation setups are summarized in Table I." No measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "The performance of the proposed MATD3 nearly approaches that of the idealized centralized TD3 even for UAV numbers not included in the training." Training uses 2 to 4 active UAVs and testing uses M in [2, 6].
q3_support: p. 11: "Naive: UAVs are randomly matched with MUs" (non-learned), "Vanila MATD3 [43]" and "MATD3 Without Initial Message [34]" (earlier learned methods), compared on total energy consumption: "Fig. 5 presents the average total energy consumption performance with varying numbers of UAVs."
q4_support: p. 7: "its computational cost is negligible" is only qualitative; p. 10 gives layer widths only. No order of complexity, parameter count, FLOPs or runtime is reported; the message size of 16 (p. 12) is signaling overhead.
q5_support: p. 10: "Our simulation setups are summarized in Table I."; the episodes come from the authors' own simulator, and the paper gives no code or data link and cites no public channel dataset.
notes: Included, area 6, but borderline. Passes above_phy only through the learned bandwidth allocation of the UAV uplinks (p. 8: "indicates the ratio of the bandwidth assigned for MU k to the maximum bandwidth"), learned jointly with association, mobility, CPU allocation and offloading ratio, which are above the physical layer (p. 8). The reviewer should confirm that this justifies area 6 rather than above_phy. q1: the model of [39] is a published analytical model, not a standardized one. Table I (p. 10) was read from the page image.
